scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The imported 1492 to 1500 polygon is unchanged and unverified. Living peoples are not assigned a fall date from that interval.

British Museum terminology documents historical inconsistency rather than authorizing the merger of distinct communities. The card concerns Akawaio; Arekuna participation is named in joint initiatives.
Museum collection dates and probable collector attributions are not dates of manufacture or excavated archaeological contexts. No first-invention claim is made.
Only the published cassava article abstract was inspected. Makushi-specific propagation details are not reassigned to Akawaio. No food-processing recipe is offered.
The dictionary credits missionaries and community participants; the card does not suggest outsiders invented the language. Local PDF page 122 is printed page 120.
Clarke’s account explicitly distinguishes the older western route from the 2001 eastern expedition. No plant discovery is falsely credited to the wrong expedition or people.

The mapping article is a 2002 report reprinted in a later collection. Its legal statements are not presented as the current legal outcome. The 2025 council report records an application, not approval.
Modern institutional examples show continuity without proving that every institution or practice existed in 1492. Independent historical review and geometry assessment remain pending.
